title: Metric sharding and SLI computation for inference KPIs
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Our current Prometheus + remote_write ingestion shows exploding cardinality for per-request inference metrics (model_version, customer_id, route, prompt_type, instance_id). This causes high CPU and storage on the ingestion tier and makes SLI calculation (p95/p99 latency and error rate per-customer) expensive and slow.

Goal: Build a pipeline that reduces raw-cardinality at ingestion, computes robust SLIs in an aggregation layer, and preserves trace linkage for root-cause (exemplars/tracing hooks). The pipeline must be compatible with existing telemetry (OTel and Prometheus remote_write) and support canary rollouts.

Scope and deliverables:
- Design and implement a lightweight metric sharder/aggregator service that sits after the OTel Collector / Prometheus remote_write receiver. The sharder will: reduce labels via configured cardinality policies, hash and route metrics to a fixed set of aggregation shards, and emit derived aggregates (sharded histograms / sum counters) to the long-term metrics store.
- Add an enrichment step that computes streaming SLIs: p50/p95/p99 token-latency histograms per model family and error-rate counters per route. Use HDR histograms (or t-digest) to keep memory predictable.
- Preserve trace linkage: continue to emit exemplars from the runtime and wire them through to shards so Grafana can link metric spikes to traces. Update tracing hooks in runtime to attach exemplar IDs when latency > p95.
- Update runtime exporters: add a low-cardinality metrics surface (model_family, region, instance_type) and emit high-cardinality debug metrics only under a sampling flag.
- Update Prometheus ingestion config (remote_write and relabel rules) and OTel Collector pipeline to route through the sharder for write-heavy clusters.
- Dashboards and alerting: new Grafana dashboards for aggregated SLIs (global and per-tenant rollups), and an alert for SLI drift and cardinality growth.

Trade-offs considered:
- Accuracy vs. cost: Bucketing histograms at the aggregation layer trades off exact per-request percentiles for much lower ingestion cost. We chose HDR histograms with configurable precision so teams can tune for accuracy.
- Sampling vs. full fidelity: For debugging we will allow debug-mode full-cardinality metrics under a sampled flag; default product telemetry will be aggregated.
- Where to compute SLIs: Doing SLIs in the pipeline reduces query-time load on Prometheus/TSDB but requires carefully versioned aggregation code and replayability for audits.

Implementation notes:
- Sharder service in Go, deployed as a horizontally-scalable K8s StatefulSet; uses a consistent-hash ring to route metric streams to N shards (configurable via Feature Flag).
- Aggregation stores intermediate histograms in RocksDB-backed local store with periodic flush to long-term TSDB (VictoriaMetrics / Cortex / ClickHouse depending on cluster).
- Use Kafka topic "metrics-aggregates" as the durable buffer between sharder and long-term storage to allow reprocessing and retention.
- OTel Collector config: add a new pipeline named "inference-agg" that routes sampled/full metrics and forwards exemplars.
- Runtime change: add a flag --emit-debug-metrics-sample-rate and an exemplar hook for high-latency spans.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch: initial sharder + aggregation unit tests and local end-to-end with synthetic traffic (PR link below).
2) Canary: deploy to staging, route 5% of production traffic via a traffic-splitting rule for two weeks. Validate SLI deltas vs. raw metrics.
3) Gradual ramp: increase to 25% and then 100% if SLI differences within +/- 3% for p95 and error rate.
4) Full switch: turn on relabel rules to drop high-cardinality metrics unless debug sampling enabled.

Observability/QA:
- Synthetic replay harness will feed 3 traffic profiles (low, bursty, multi-tenant) and validate histogram accuracy and exemplar linkage.
- Add unit/integration tests around histogram aggregation and label-reduction policies.

Success criteria:
- 60% reduction in cardinality for Prometheus ingestion in the targeted clusters during normal workloads.
- Computed SLIs (p95 & error rate) available in Grafana with <5s lag and within 3% of replayed raw-percentiles in test runs.
- Exemplar-to-trace linkage working for >95% of exemplar-emitting requests.

Notes and open questions:
- Which long-term TSDB is the canonical store for derived SLIs? (Eng lead preference: VictoriaMetrics for write-heavy clusters, ClickHouse for analytical queries.)
- How do we version aggregation logic for audits? Plan: include aggregation version in metric labels and persist aggregator config in Git.
- Security: ensure sharder has least-privilege access to Kafka and storage.
acceptance_criteria: Sharder service deployed in staging and can process synthetic workload without crashing
SLIs (p95/p99 and error rate) computed by aggregation pipeline match replayed raw metrics within 3% for p95 and 1% for error rate
Grafana dashboards display aggregated SLIs and exemplar links to traces
Cardinality measured and documented; >60% reduction observed in target cluster
Canary plan executed and documented with rollback instructions

Implement sharder service and consistent-hash routing
Add HDR histogram aggregation and persistence
Wire OTel Collector pipeline and update Prometheus relabel rules
Update runtime exporters to emit low-cardinality metrics and exemplar hooks
Create synthetic traffic harness and run validation
Execute canary rollout and document results
